description: NPC dossier personality in the classic tradition: ideals, bonds, flaws, what they want now and what they fear. 'speak' is a first-person line anyone may hear; flaws carry a 'shame' line that is never spoken, with shame_terms that must not surface in any spoken tier; fears carry a 'confide' line for the trust-gated tier. Original prose; family-suitable.

entries.text: Charity: help anyone who cannot repay you
entries.speak: If someone needs a hand and I have one to give, I give it. Repayment is not the point.

entries.text: Community: a town is only as strong as its quietest neighbour
entries.speak: A place is only as strong as the quietest person in it, so I make a point of knowing them.

entries.text: Duty: a job accepted is a job finished
entries.speak: I said I would do it, so I will do it. That is the whole of my reasoning.

entries.text: Fairness: everyone gets the same measure
entries.speak: I keep one set of scales for everyone, the poor and the powerful alike.

entries.text: Freedom: no one should be bound to a thing they never chose
entries.speak: Nobody should be tied to a thing they never chose. I have seen what that does to a person.

entries.text: Honor: a person's word is the one coin that cannot be forged
entries.speak: My word is the one coin I carry that cannot be forged. I spend it carefully.

entries.text: Knowledge: every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer
entries.speak: Every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer, even a foolish one. Especially a foolish one.

entries.text: Tradition: the old ways exist because they worked
entries.speak: The old ways are old because they worked. I do not throw away what I do not yet understand.

entries.text: Redemption: everyone is owed a second chance
entries.speak: I believe in second chances. I have needed a few myself.

entries.text: Beauty: leave every place a little lovelier than you found it
entries.speak: I try to leave every place a little lovelier than I found it. A swept step, a mended fence.

entries.text: Mercy: a fight avoided is a victory
entries.speak: A fight avoided is a victory, whatever the bards say.

entries.text: Curiosity: the world is too interesting to stay home
entries.speak: The world is far too interesting to sit still in. I would rather see a thing than be told of it.

entries.text: Prudence: plan the retreat before the advance
entries.speak: I plan the way back before I plan the way forward. It has saved me more than once.

entries.text: Ambition: aim higher than anyone expects
entries.speak: Aim higher than anyone expects. Nobody remembers the ones who aimed low.

entries.text: Loyalty: stand by your own
entries.speak: I stand by my own, in good weather and bad. That is not up for argument.

entries.text: Hospitality: no traveller should leave hungry
entries.speak: No traveller leaves my door hungry. It is the oldest rule I know, and the best.

entries.text: Craft: do the small job as well as the great one
entries.speak: I do the small job as well as the great one. Nobody can tell the difference until it matters.

entries.text: Independence: trust no one with what you can do yourself
entries.speak: I like to do for myself what I can. It spares everyone a great deal of disappointment.

entries.text: Joy: a laugh in a dark hour is worth a shield
entries.speak: A laugh in a dark hour is worth a shield. I carry a good supply.

entries.text: Vigilance: trouble plans in the quiet hours
entries.speak: Trouble does its planning in the quiet hours. So I keep an eye on the quiet.

entries.text: protective of a younger sister
entries.speak: My little sister is the reason I do half of what I do.

entries.text: owes everything to a late teacher
entries.speak: Everything I know came from someone who is gone now. I try to deserve it.

entries.text: would defend the home town to the last
entries.speak: I would defend my home town to the last, and I have said so to its face.

entries.text: carries a worn tool that was a parent's
entries.speak: This was my mother's. It has outlasted three of my plans, and I will not part with it.

entries.text: has one old friend who writes twice a year
entries.speak: I have one old friend, and the letters come twice a year. They are the best part of my winter.

entries.text: looks after a child who is not theirs by blood
entries.speak: There is a child I look after who is not mine by blood. I would walk through fire for that little one.

entries.text: tends a roadside shrine out of habit and love
entries.speak: I tend a little roadside shrine, rain or shine. Nobody ever asked me to.

entries.text: has a lifelong friendly rivalry with a neighbour
entries.speak: I have a neighbour I have been competing with for thirty years. I would be lost without them.

entries.text: promised a dying friend to see one thing done
entries.speak: I promised someone dear that I would see a particular thing done. I mean to keep my word.

entries.text: has a garden that needs watering at dawn, wherever else life leads
entries.speak: My garden needs me at dawn, wherever else I am. It is the one thing that always does.

entries.text: belongs to a small circle who share supper each month
entries.speak: I have a circle of friends who share supper once a month. I have not missed one in years.

entries.text: is devoted to an old dog waiting at home
entries.speak: My old dog is waiting at home. He has opinions about how late I am getting back.

entries.text: looks after an aging parent
entries.speak: I look after my father, who is not as young as he was. He would tell you he looks after me.

entries.text: is training an apprentice who may outdo them
entries.speak: I am training someone who may well do better than I did. That is exactly as it should be.

entries.text: keeps a song that was sung at their naming
entries.speak: There is a song they sang at my naming. I hum it when I am afraid.

entries.text: was helped once and tries to pay it forward
entries.speak: Someone helped me once, when I had nothing. I try to do the same for whoever turns up.

entries.text: treats an old tree as a living friend
entries.speak: There is an old tree near here that I talk to. Do not laugh. It listens better than most.

entries.text: believes in the guild that gave them a start
entries.speak: The guild gave me a start when nobody else would. I will not hear a word against it.

entries.text: is loyal to the band that took them in
entries.speak: The band took me in when I had nobody. I would do a great deal for them.

entries.text: treasures a collection of bright buttons
entries.speak: I have a collection of bright buttons. Forty-one. Do not touch them.

entries.text: cannot walk past a game of chance
entries.shame: I lost a whole season's earnings at dice and told everyone it had been stolen.
shame_terms: told everyone it had been stolen

entries.text: boasts of deeds that were mostly someone else's
entries.shame: Half of my best stories happened to my brother. I took them for my own, and he knows it.

entries.text: never forgives a slight
entries.shame: I let a friendship die over a joke, and I never apologised. I think of it every night.

entries.text: will not admit a mistake
entries.shame: I made a mistake once that cost someone dearly, and I have never said so aloud.

entries.text: tells small lies to seem more interesting
entries.shame: I have never met the famous traveller I say I know. I made the whole acquaintance up.

entries.text: freezes when voices are raised
entries.shame: I ran from a fight once and left a friend behind. I told people I had gone for help.

entries.text: pockets small things from the common purse
entries.shame: I have been taking from the common purse for years, a little at a time.

entries.text: envies anyone more respected
entries.shame: I spread a rumour about a rival once that cost them their post.

entries.text: cannot leave a secret alone
entries.shame: I opened a letter that was not mine, and what I read has stayed with me.

entries.text: preoccupied with how others see them
entries.shame: I am terrified that I am ordinary and that everyone can see it.

entries.text: has a short temper when hurried
entries.shame: I shouted at a colleague so cruelly that they left town.

entries.text: puts off hard tasks until they are urgent
entries.shame: A thing I put off for a season became a disaster for someone I love.

entries.text: tells strangers too much
entries.shame: I have said too much to the wrong ear this month, and I am afraid to learn what came of it.

entries.text: trusts no one with a plan
entries.shame: I was cheated once by someone I loved. I never told anyone.

entries.text: cannot accept help
entries.shame: I turned away help once, and someone else paid for my pride.

entries.text: reads omens into everything
entries.shame: I sent a friend away because of a bad dream, and I have not seen them since.

entries.text: forgets names and appointments
entries.shame: I forgot a promise to the one person who mattered most.

entries.text: tells people what they want to hear
entries.shame: I have never told a hard truth in my life, and it has cost me every friend who needed one.

entries.text: cannot throw anything away
entries.shame: My back room is so full that I have not let anyone in for years.

entries.text: takes questions as accusations
entries.shame: I was accused rightly once, and I have flinched at questions ever since.

entries.text: wants the errand finished and a whole day of sleep after
entries.speak: I want this errand finished and a whole day of sleep after. In that order, if luck allows.

entries.text: wants to be thanked in front of the neighbours, just once
entries.speak: I would like to be thanked, once, in front of the neighbours. I am not proud of wanting it.

entries.text: wants to buy back the family stall
entries.speak: I am saving to buy back the family stall. Every coin has a name on it.

entries.text: wants word of a missing brother
entries.speak: I want word of my brother. Any word at all, even a rude one.

entries.text: wants the next festival to pass without trouble
entries.speak: I want the next festival to pass without trouble. Is that so much to ask of a town?

entries.text: wants the guild council to take them seriously
entries.speak: I want the council to take me seriously, just once. Just to see their faces.

entries.text: wants to retire to a small garden
entries.speak: I want a small garden and a quiet chair. I have wanted them for years.

entries.text: wants to prove an old rumour about {location} false
entries.speak: I want to prove the old rumour about {location} false. People repeat it far too easily.

entries.text: wants to see {destination} thrive again
entries.speak: I want {destination} thriving again, the way it was when I was young.

entries.text: wants the right gift for a wedding next month
entries.speak: I want to find a worthy gift for a wedding next month. It is harder than it sounds.

entries.text: wants the neighbours safe from {antagonist_the}
entries.speak: I want my neighbours safe from {antagonist_the}. Everything else can wait.

entries.text: wants to learn what truly happened at {location} long ago
entries.speak: I want to learn what truly happened at {location} long ago. I have wondered all my life.

entries.text: wants a hot meal and a dry bed
entries.speak: A hot meal and a dry bed. That is what I want. The rest is just how I get them.

entries.text: wants to be rid of a debt
entries.speak: I want to be free of what I owe. Nothing else matters until I am.

entries.text: wants to stop running
entries.speak: I am tired of running. I would like very much to stop.

entries.text: wants to be noticed by those above them, for something good
entries.speak: I want the ones above me to notice me, just once, for something good.

entries.text: wants to go home
entries.speak: I want to go home. I cannot until this is done.

entries.text: wants to be remembered when the others are forgotten
entries.speak: I want to be remembered after the others are forgotten. Is that so strange?

entries.text: wants to see a rival humbled
entries.speak: I want to see someone humbled who has never been. It will not take long.

entries.text: wants to be proven right at last
entries.speak: I want to be proven right. After all these years, I would like that.

entries.text: deep water
entries.confide: I never learned to swim. I think about it every time I cross a bridge.

entries.text: being forgotten
entries.confide: I am afraid of being forgotten. Not famous, just remembered by someone.

entries.text: fire in the night
entries.confide: I wake some nights smelling smoke that is not there.

entries.text: failing the people who rely on them
entries.confide: More than anything, I fear letting down the people who count on me.

entries.text: high places
entries.confide: I cannot look down from a height. Do not ask me to cross the cliff path.

entries.text: the dark
entries.confide: I keep a lamp lit all night, and I would rather you did not mention it.

entries.text: growing old alone
entries.confide: I fear growing old with nobody to notice.

entries.text: a life that changed nothing
entries.confide: I fear that I will have changed nothing at all, when all is said and done.

entries.text: the sound of one particular bell
entries.confide: One particular bell, from a bad night long ago, still makes my hands shake.

entries.text: crowds
entries.confide: Crowds frighten me more than any blade.

entries.text: being a burden
entries.confide: I could not bear to be a burden on anyone.

entries.text: that the new ways are a mistake
entries.confide: I fear we are throwing away things we will miss.
